prompt: I've been caring for my mother for so long that I don't feel much anymore. I do everything that needs to be done, but I feel emotionally numb. Is this normal, and what can I do about it?
Sometimes I resent my father because caregiving has taken over my life. Then I feel horrible for thinking that. I love him, but I don't know how to deal with these feelings.
My husband is still here, but our relationship feels so different since his care needs increased. I miss the way things used to be, and I feel guilty admitting that. I don't know how to process it.
Everyone asks how my mother is doing, but nobody asks how I am. I feel invisible in my own family. I don't even know how to ask someone to notice that I'm struggling.
I managed the appointments, meals, and problems all day, and then I started crying over something small. I think I've been holding everything together for too long. What do I do tonight?
I get jealous when I see friends going on trips or enjoying weekends. I can't do those things anymore, and then I feel selfish for being jealous. I don't know how to stop comparing my life to theirs.
I've been snapping at my father and I'm afraid caregiving is turning me into a person I don't want to be. I feel ashamed of how I act when I'm exhausted.
I keep thinking about how much worse things might get with my mother's condition. I can't stop imagining the future, and it's making it difficult to get through today.
My days are full of caregiving tasks, but I feel incredibly lonely. I barely have conversations that aren't about care. I don't know how to reconnect with people when I have so little time.
I know I need help, but admitting it makes me feel like I've failed. I keep telling people I'm fine even though I'm struggling to cope. How do I get past that?
My father couldn't do something he used to do easily today. It was a small thing, but it hit me hard. I feel like I'm grieving changes that keep happening while he's still here.
I'm angry that caregiving has fallen mostly on me while everyone else continues their life. I know anger isn't going to fix anything, but I can't seem to let it go.
Even when someone else is looking after my mother, I can't relax. I keep checking my phone and feel guilty doing anything enjoyable. How can I learn to take a real break?
I used to have hobbies, goals, and things I looked forward to. Now everything revolves around caregiving. I don't know what I enjoy anymore or who I am outside this role.
I'm having a really hard day. I don't want advice or a checklist right now. I just need somewhere to say how exhausted and upset I am without being told to stay positive.
I want to go to a friend's birthday dinner, but I feel guilty leaving my father for a few hours. I feel like wanting a normal evening makes me selfish.
I'm so tired that even deciding what to do next feels impossible. Nothing is an emergency, but there are too many things on my mind. Can you help me slow down without giving me a huge plan?
My mother said something really hurtful to me today. I know she may not fully understand what she's saying, but it still hurts. I feel bad for taking it personally.
I had a good afternoon away from caregiving and felt happy for a while. Then I came home and felt guilty for enjoying myself while my husband is struggling. How can I deal with that?
I feel like I'm reaching my limit. I'm exhausted, increasingly irritable, and afraid I can't keep doing this the way I have been. I need help figuring out what to do before things get worse.
